passage: Every evening when Jagdish's mother, Preeti, got home, he had his blocks ready to show her. Today the baby started crying just as Jagdish was placing the top block, and Preeti ran to the cot. Jagdish stood there, holding the block. Nobody looked at his tower. He swept it over with his arm and the blocks clattered across the floor. Preeti turned. "Oh, Jagdish. You want me too, don't you?" She handed him the baby's wipes. "Please pass me those." Later she sat with him alone to rebuild the tower.

qa.q: What did Jagdish sweep over with his arm?
qa.a: He swept his tower over with his arm.

qa.q: Why did Jagdish knock down the tower?
qa.a: He felt forgotten because his mother ran to the baby, and knocking it over was a way to be noticed.

qa.q: What did Preeti do that helps Jagdish feel seen?
qa.a: She said aloud that he wanted her too, gave him a small job passing the wipes, and later sat with him alone to rebuild the tower.

qa.q: How might Preeti feel when the tower crashes while she is soothing the baby?
qa.a: She is probably stretched between two children and tired. Her gentle words show she understands why he did it.

grounding: When the baby cries my parent runs to him and I feel forgotten and act out; a small job and time together help me feel seen.

passage:
Note for Varun's teacher, from his papa, Amandeep.
Since baby Kiran came home, every time Kiran cries, I run to him. Varun then throws his spoon or climbs the cupboard, and looks straight at me. I think he feels forgotten. You may see some of this at school. This week we gave Varun a job: he brings the clean nappy when Kiran cries. After dinner we have ten minutes of "Varun time", just us and his puzzles. Last night he said, "My time!" and hugged me. We will keep going.

qa.q: What job did Varun get when Kiran cries?
qa.a: He brings the clean nappy when Kiran cries.

qa.q: Why might Varun throw his spoon and look straight at his papa?
qa.a: He feels forgotten and left out when the baby gets attention, so acting out is a way to be noticed.

qa.q: What did Amandeep try that helped Varun feel seen?
qa.a: He gave Varun a small job and a daily ten minutes of Varun time with puzzles, just the two of them.

qa.q: If you were Varun's teacher, how could this note help you?
qa.a: It explains Varun's behaviour, so the teacher can be patient and give him small moments of attention at school too.

grounding: A parent notices his older child feels forgotten when the baby cries, and responds with a small job and special daily time.

passage: Every night the baby cried and Amma, Minakshi, hurried to him with the lamp. Noor lay alone on the mat. One night she tipped over the water pot with a clang. Amma turned. "Noor!" Noor's eyes filled up. "You always go to him." Amma was quiet. Then she said, "You're right, I've been busy. Come, you hold the lamp while I rock him." Noor held it high and steady. The next evening, Amma took her up to the roof steps. "This is our time," she said, pointing at the stars. Noor leaned on her shoulder.

qa.q: What did Noor tip over with a clang?
qa.a: Noor tipped over the water pot.

qa.q: What was Noor feeling when she said "You always go to him"?
qa.a: She felt forgotten and hurt, left alone on the mat while the baby got all the attention.

qa.q: What two things did Minakshi do that helped Noor feel seen?
qa.a: She gave Noor the job of holding the lamp and began a special time on the roof steps together.

qa.q: How does Minakshi see the tipped water pot once Noor explains?
qa.a: She understands it as a sign that Noor feels left out, not just naughtiness, and admits she has been busy.

grounding: A young girl feels forgotten when her mother rushes to the crying baby, acts out, and her mother responds with a job and special time.
